questions.stem: Suppose your university student union is planning to hold a speech contest. You are now to write a proposal for organizing the contest. The proposal may include the topic, aim , procedure and selection of contestants. You will have 30 minutes to write the proposal. You should write at least 120 words but no more than 180 words.
questions.analysis:
【参考范文】
A Proposal for a Speech Contest

On behalf of the Student Union, I am writing to propose that our university hold a campus speech contest next month, and the details are outlined below for your approval.

The contest will focus on the theme "My Chinese Dream." Our aim is to sharpen students' public-speaking skills, build their confidence, and enrich campus cultural life.

As for the procedure, we will first post a notice to call for entries. Then a preliminary round will be held in each college. Finally, twelve finalists will deliver their speeches on stage, scored by a panel of teachers and students.

The selection of contestants will be fair and open: applicants must submit a written draft, and those with clear ideas and fluent expression will be shortlisted through a short interview. We sincerely hope you will approve this proposal, and any suggestions would be warmly welcomed.

The Student Union

sections.title: Section II Listening Comprehension
sections.note: 听力为历年真题原文，题目与答案为官方标准答案；在线音频由语音合成朗读原文，不是考场录音；换浏览器、换手机都能播。

transcript.text: A 22-year-old Chinese woman who suffered from a persistent cough was shocked to learn that she had a piece of chicken bone lodged in her lung.
transcript.zh: 一名22岁的中国女性因持续咳嗽而震惊地得知,她的肺部卡着一块鸡骨头。

transcript.text: The unnamed woman, from the province of Shandong, started to have coughing problems when she was 7 or 8 years old. For 14 years, she made numerous hospital visits. However, no doctor could identify any problem. Her uncontrollable coughing was a mystery.
transcript.zh: 这名来自山东省的未透露姓名的女性,在7岁或8岁时开始出现咳嗽问题。14年来,她多次前往医院就诊。然而,没有一位医生能够发现任何问题。她无法控制的咳嗽一直是个谜。

transcript.text: Finally, the woman got a full body scan at a hospital in the city of Qingdao. This special medical procedure revealed she had a chicken bone stuck in her lung. Doctors performed surgery and removed the bone. The simple procedure went smoothly and the woman has recovered fully. With the bone finally removed from her lung, the woman is very happy that she no longer suffers from that annoying cough.
transcript.zh: 最终,这名女性在青岛市的一家医院进行了全身扫描。这项特殊的医疗检查显示她的肺部卡着一块鸡骨头。医生进行了手术并取出了骨头。这个简单的手术进行得很顺利,女性已完全康复。随着骨头最终从肺部取出,这名女性非常高兴,因为她不再遭受那恼人的咳嗽困扰。

questions.stem: What was the woman's problem?

options.text: She was pierced by a chicken bone.
She was coughing all the time.

questions.analysis: 细节题。答案句（P2）：The unnamed woman, from the province of Shandong, started to have coughing problems when she was 7 or 8 years old. For 14 years, she made numerous hospital visits. However, no doctor could identify any problem. Her uncontrollable coughing was a mystery.信号：反复强调的核心症状即答案句 。判定她问题是什么，要抓原文反复落在同一件事上的那句。第 2 段 started to have coughing problems、Her uncontrollable coughing…

optionAnalysis.A: 原词陷阱：选项 She was pierced by a chicken bone. 借用了原文确实念到的 a piece of chicken bone，听到 chicken bone 很容易手一抖就选。但原文说的是鸡骨头卡在肺里，是导致咳嗽的原因，而且并非 pierced（刺穿）；题问的是她表现出的问题——咳嗽，不是病因，故 A 答非所问。 借用原文：lodged in her lung
optionAnalysis.C: 原词陷阱：选项 She suffered from lung cancer. 蹭了原文反复出现的 lung（肺），把肺里有东西夸大成肺癌。原文通篇只说咳嗽和鸡骨头，根本没出现 cancer 一词，这是把听到的 lung 顺手脑补成重病的陷阱。 借用原文：was shocked to learn
optionAnalysis.D: 原词陷阱：选项 She suffered from shock. 借了原文 was shocked to learn（得知时大为震惊）里的 shock。但原文的 shocked 指她得知真相时很吃惊这一情绪反应，不是她患的疾病；题问她的问题（毛病），故 D 张冠李戴、答非所问。
optionAnalysis.B: 正确项：与答案句同义替换（coughing problems ↔ coughing all the time 同义改写：咳嗽的毛病等于一直在咳）

questions.evidenceText: The unnamed woman, from the province of Shandong, started to have coughing problems when she was 7 or 8 years old. For 14 years, she made numerous hospital visits. However, no doctor could identify any problem. Her uncontrollable coughing was a mystery.

questions.stem: How was the woman's problem eventually solved?
questions.analysis: 细节题。答案句（P3）：Doctors performed surgery and removed the bone.信号：结尾处交代最终处置的动作句 。问最终怎么解决，答案信号是叙事收束段里那句表最后做了什么的动作句。第 3 段先靠扫描查出病因，紧接 Doctors performed surgery and removed the b…

optionAnalysis.A: 原词陷阱：选项 By eating chicken soup daily. 蹭了原文反复出现的 chicken（来自 a piece of chicken bone），把鸡骨头致病偷换成天天喝鸡汤治病。原文根本没提任何喝汤、食疗，这是靠 chicken 撞词制造的听到鸡就选陷阱。 借用原文：A 22-year-old Chinese woman
optionAnalysis.B: 未提及：选项 Through regular exercising. 说靠规律锻炼解决，但原文从开头到结尾只字未提运动锻炼。它利用的是考生生病要多锻炼的生活常识，诱你用常识替代原文，属于原文未提及。
optionAnalysis.D: 原词陷阱：选项 By using traditional Chinese medicine. 里的 Chinese 和原文 A 22-year-old Chinese woman 的 Chinese 撞词，让人以为中国人就用中医。但原文交代的解决手段明明是 performed surgery（手术），全篇没提任何中医草药，这是借 Chinese 撞词加常识联想的双重陷阱。
optionAnalysis.C: 正确项：与答案句同义替换（Doctors performed surgery ↔ Through a surgical operation 同根改写：做手术等于通过外科手术）

questions.evidenceText: Doctors performed surgery and removed the bone.

transcript.text: 1 A white sheep named Prickles that ran away from an Australian farm during the 2013 bushfires, recently returned home. 2 According to farmer Alice Gray, Prickles was only a lamb when she ran away.
The bushfires that hit the area back then destroyed a large part of her family's massive property.
They thought Prickles had died in the fire.
But instead, the young sheep escaped into a 200-acre forest near the farm.
Once the fires were over, the family had to fix the damage done to the farm, as it was such a large property.
This included rebuilding about 50 kilometers of fencing.
It was this huge fencing that prevented Prickles from finding her way back.
Over the years, the family spotted her a few times.
They even recorded her with cameras installed to monitor deer activity.
But while they knew Prickles was alive, they couldn't find her and never expected her to return by herself.
Seven years later, they were proven wrong.

questions.stem: What does the news report say about the white sheep Prickles?

options.text: It was Alice Gray's lovely pet.
It got injured in a big bushfire.
It ran away into a nearby forest.

questions.analysis: 细节题。答案句（P1）：A white sheep named Prickles that ran away from an Australian farm during the 2013 bushfires, recently returned home.信号：新闻首句即核心事实 。新闻短消息的第一句通常就把最关键的事实交代清楚。这里开篇 A white sheep named Prickles that ran away from an Australian farm d…

optionAnalysis.A: 原词陷阱：选项说羊 It was born 13 years ago.，但录音只提到 "2013 bushfires" 这个火灾年份，从没说羊出生于 13 年前——它把年份信息张冠李戴到 "出生" 上，专骗听到年数就对号入座的人。 借用原文：According to farmer Alice Gray
optionAnalysis.B: 原词陷阱：选项称羊是 It was Alice Gray's lovely pet.，录音里 According to farmer Alice Gray 确实出现了 Alice Gray，但她是农场主、是消息来源，录音从没说这羊是她的 "宠物"——这是借真实人名编造的关系。 借用原文：escaped into a 200-acre forest near the farm
optionAnalysis.C: 原词陷阱：选项说羊 It got injured in a big bushfire.，"bushfire" 是录音反复出现的原词，听到就想选；但录音说的是羊 escaped into a 200-acre forest 逃走并活了下来，从没说它在火中受伤，"injured" 是无中生有。
optionAnalysis.D: 正确项：与答案句同义替换（ran away from an Australian farm ↔ ran away into a nearby forest 同一逃走动作的去向补全）

questions.evidenceText: A white sheep named Prickles that ran away from an Australian farm during the 2013 bushfires, recently returned home.

questions.stem: What did the family do after the bushfires?

options.text: They rebuilt the fencing around their farm.
They spent seven years replanting their farm.
They claimed damages for their heavy losses.
They installed a camera to monitor sheep activity.

questions.analysis: 细节题。答案句（P2）：Once the fires were over, the family had to fix the damage done to the farm, as it was such a large property. This included rebuilding about 50 kilometers of fencing.信号：时间信号词 Once the fires were over 。答案句由时间信号 Once the fires were over（大火一过）引出，正好对上题干的 "after the bushfires"。这个时间…

optionAnalysis.B: 原词陷阱：选项说 They spent seven years replanting their farm.，"seven years" 是录音原词，但录音里 Seven years later, they were proven wrong 的七年指的是 "羊七年后回来"，不是 "花七年补种农场"，"replanting" 录音根本没提，是张冠李戴加无中生有。 借用原文：destroyed a large part of her family's massive property
optionAnalysis.C: 未提及：选项称 They claimed damages for their heavy losses.，录音确实说山火 destroyed a large part of her family's massive property 造成了损失，听到 "损失" 容易顺势联想到 "索赔"，但录音从头到尾没说他们去索赔，"claimed damages" 是凭损失情节脑补出来的。 借用原文：cameras installed to monitor deer activity
optionAnalysis.D: 偷换概念：选项说 They installed a camera to monitor sheep activity.，录音里 cameras installed to monitor deer activity 确实有装摄像头，但监控的是 "deer（鹿）" 不是 "sheep（羊）"，选项只改了一个名词就把意思偷换了，专骗听到 "camera/monitor" 就选的人。
optionAnalysis.A: 正确项：与答案句同义替换（rebuilding about 50 kilometers of fencing ↔ rebuilt the fencing around their farm 同一重建围栏动作的概括）

questions.evidenceText: Once the fires were over, the family had to fix the damage done to the farm, as it was such a large property. This included rebuilding about 50 kilometers of fencing.

transcript.text: Tons of gold have fallen out of the sky in Russia after a cargo plane malfunctioned in midair this morning.
transcript.zh: 今天上午，一架货机在空中发生故障后，数吨黄金从俄罗斯天空坠落。

transcript.text: The aircraft was carrying 265 million pounds worth of gold and diamonds, when the door flew open—sending the precious metal back to earth.
transcript.zh: 这架飞机载有价值2.65亿英镑的黄金和钻石，当舱门突然打开时，贵重金属被抛回地面。

transcript.text: According to the official news agency, Russian authorities have recovered more than 170 gold bars weighing 20 kilograms each. The plane was traveling from Yakutsk Airport in a major diamond-producing region to the city Krasnoyarsk in Siberia.
transcript.zh: 据官方通讯社报道，俄罗斯当局已经回收了超过170根金条，每根重20公斤。该飞机从主要钻石产区的Yakutsk机场飞往西伯利亚的Krasnoyarsk市。

transcript.text: However, the aircraft made an emergency landing in Magan after it began losing some of its valuable cargo.
transcript.zh: 然而，这架飞机在开始丢失部分贵重货物后，在Magan紧急降落。

transcript.text: Reports suggest some bars of gold were scattered up to 15 miles away from the airport. Nine tons of gold on plane AN-12 belonged to a goldmine company.
transcript.zh: 报道称，一些金条散落在距离机场15英里远的地方。AN-12飞机上的9吨黄金属于一家金矿公司。

transcript.text: Police have sealed off the runway, and say it is unclear if it was an accident or an attempted robbery. Technical engineers who worked on the plane prior to take-off are reportedly going to be questioned by the police.
transcript.zh: 警方已经封锁了跑道，并表示尚不清楚这是一起事故还是抢劫未遂。据报道，起飞前在飞机上工作的技术工程师将接受警方问询。

questions.stem: What is the news report mainly about?

options.text: The disappearance of some gold and diamonds.
The transfer of tons of precious metal by air.
The crash of a Russian cargo airplane.
The loss of gold from an airplane.

questions.analysis: 主旨题。答案句（P1）：Tons of gold have fallen out of the sky in Russia after a cargo plane malfunctioned in midair this morning.信号：新闻首句即点题 。新闻短消息的核心动作往往压在开头第一句，本则的首句 Tons of gold have fallen out of the sky in Russia after a cargo plane mal…

optionAnalysis.A: 原词陷阱：A 盗用了录音里的 gold 和 diamonds 两个原词，听着很耳熟，但它说的是 The disappearance of some gold and diamonds.（金子钻石的消失），"消失"指不知去向，而录音明确是"从飞机上掉落"且大部分已被寻回，方向不符，也漏掉了"飞机"这个关键。 借用原文：265 million pounds worth of gold and diamonds
optionAnalysis.B: 答非所问：B 的 The transfer of tons of precious metal by air.（用飞机空运大量贵金属）确实是事情的背景，precious metal、by air 也都能在录音里找到影子，但它只描述了"正在空运"这个前提，完全没提"出故障、金子掉落"这个真正的新闻点，以偏概全。 借用原文：the aircraft made an emergency landing in Magan
optionAnalysis.C: 过度推断：C 说 The crash of a Russian cargo airplane.（俄罗斯货机坠毁），Russian、cargo airplane 都是原词，但录音里飞机是 made an emergency landing（紧急迫降）而非坠毁，crash 把事故程度夸大了，与事实相反。
optionAnalysis.D: 正确项：与答案句同义替换（Tons of gold have fallen out of the sky ↔ The loss of gold from an airplane. 金子掉落=金子丢失）

questions.evidenceText: Tons of gold have fallen out of the sky in Russia after a cargo plane malfunctioned in midair this morning.

questions.stem: What did the aircraft do when the incident happened?

options.text: It informed the local police at once.
It had a crew member fix the problem.

questions.analysis: 细节题。答案句（P4）：However, the aircraft made an emergency landing in Magan after it began losing some of its valuable cargo.信号：转折 However 后是落点 。本句以转折词 However 起头——前文一直在讲金子掉了、被寻回多少，转折之后才交代飞机本身的应对动作 made an emergency landing，转折后的句子正是本题答案句。

optionAnalysis.B: 张冠李戴：B 说 It informed the local police at once.（飞机立刻通知了当地警方），police 一词录音确实念到了，但录音是 Police have sealed off the runway（警方封锁跑道），是警方主动介入，并没有"飞机通知警方"这回事，张冠李戴。 借用原文：belonged to a goldmine company
optionAnalysis.C: 原词陷阱：C 说 It contacted the goldmine company.（飞机联系了金矿公司），goldmine company 是原词，但录音只说 Nine tons of gold on plane AN-12 belonged to a goldmine company（飞机上九吨金子归一家金矿公司所有），金矿公司只是货物的主人，根本没说飞机去联系它。
optionAnalysis.D: 未提及：D 说 It had a crew member fix the problem.（飞机让机组人员修好了故障），录音确实提到 malfunctioned（故障）和后文的 technical engineers（技术工程师），听着像"有人修"，但录音里飞机是迫降处理，从没说让机组成员在空中把问题修好了，纯属无中生有。
optionAnalysis.A: 正确项：与答案句同义替换（the aircraft made an emergency landing ↔ It made an emergency landing. 几乎原句对应）

questions.evidenceText: However, the aircraft made an emergency landing in Magan after it began losing some of its valuable cargo.

questions.stem: What does the news report say about the technical engineers who worked on the plane before take-off?

options.text: They will cooperate with the police.
They had checked the plane carefully.
They will be questioned by the police.
They took some gold bars and diamonds.

questions.analysis: 细节题。答案句（P6）：Technical engineers who worked on the plane prior to take-off are reportedly going to be questioned by the police.信号：末段交代相关人员后续 。新闻把对涉事人员的后续处置放在结尾，末段 Technical engineers... are reportedly going to be questioned by the police …

optionAnalysis.A: 与原文相反：A 说 They will cooperate with the police.（他们将配合警方），police 是原词且"将来 + 警方"的框架很像，但录音是 be questioned by the police（被警方问询，被动），工程师是被调查的对象，并非主动配合，主被动方向被偷换。 借用原文：it is unclear if it was an accident or an attempted robbery
optionAnalysis.B: 未提及：B 说 They had checked the plane carefully.（他们已仔细检查过飞机），借工程师 worked on the plane 联想出"检查"，但录音只说工程师"起飞前做过工作"且"将被问询"，从没说他们"仔细检查过"，更没说检查得是否仔细，无中生有。
optionAnalysis.D: 过度推断：D 说 They took some gold bars and diamonds.（他们拿走了金条和钻石），gold bars、diamonds 全是原词，又借录音 it is unclear if it was an accident or an attempted robbery（尚不清楚是事故还是抢劫未遂）的联想，把工程师直接坐实成偷窃者，但录音只说"将被问询"、尚未定性，是过度推断。
optionAnalysis.C: 正确项：与答案句同义替换（are reportedly going to be questioned by the police ↔ They will be questioned by the police. 将被警方问询，几乎同句）

questions.evidenceText: Technical engineers who worked on the plane prior to take-off are reportedly going to be questioned by the police.

transcript.text: M: Hello, you're through to customer service. This is Michael speaking. Before we continue, I just want to make you aware that this call is being recorded and may be used in the future for training purposes. What can I help you with today?
transcript.zh: M: 您好,您已接通客户服务部。我是Michael。在我们继续之前,我想提醒您,本通话正在录音,未来可能用于培训目的。请问有什么可以帮您的?

transcript.text: W: Hi, my name is Jean Seimon. I recently bought an office chair from your company, but I returned it about a week ago. I'm just calling to inquire when I will be able to get my money back. It says on your website that your company will pay back the money within three working days of you receiving the returned item. But it's been five working days and I haven't received anything.
transcript.zh: W: 您好,我叫Jean Seimon。我最近从贵公司买了一把办公椅,但大约一周前退了货。我打电话是想询问什么时候能拿到退款。贵公司网站上说,在收到退货后三个工作日内会退款。但已经过了五个工作日了,我还没收到任何款项。

transcript.text: M: I'm sorry to hear that, Miss Seimon. What's your customer reference number, please?
transcript.zh: M: 很抱歉听到这个情况, Seimon女士。请问您的客户编号是多少?

transcript.text: M: Okay, 389460. I'm just looking on the system here. And according to our records, the chair you returned was received by our warehouse on Friday morning. The payment was made on Wednesday. But this seems to be a problem with your card number.
transcript.zh: M: 好的,389460。我这就在系统里查一下。根据我们的记录,您退回的椅子是周五上午被我们仓库收到的。退款是在周三处理的。但您的卡号似乎有问题。

transcript.text: W: My card number? Oh, maybe it has something to do with my new card. It was sent to me on Tuesday. Maybe the bank canceled my old one before you've made the payment.
transcript.zh: W: 我的卡号?哦,可能跟我的新卡有关。周二才寄给我的。也许银行在你们付款之前把我的旧卡注销了。

transcript.text: M: Well, you'll need to update your card details directly on our website. Just make sure you're logged in. And then under the description of your personal information, you should see an option for updating payment methods.
transcript.zh: M: 那您需要直接在我们网站上更新您的银行卡信息。确保您已经登录,然后在个人信息栏下面,应该能看到更新付款方式的选项。

transcript.text: W: I am logged in, and I'll give that a go.
transcript.zh: W: 我已经登录了,我试试看。

transcript.text: M: I'll make a note here on the system for you, so that the payment will be made tomorrow morning.
transcript.zh: M: 我会在系统里给您做个备注,这样明天上午就能给您退款。

transcript.text: W: Thank you very much.
transcript.zh: W: 非常感谢。

questions.stem: Why does the man have his conversation with the woman recorded?
questions.analysis: 细节题。答案句（P1）：I just want to make you aware that this call is being recorded and may be used in the future for training purposes.信号：目的状语 for...purposes 。答案信号是表目的的短语 used in the future for training purposes——"录音"这一动作后面紧跟的"for... purposes"就是它…

optionAnalysis.A: 原词陷阱：选项 For the company's records. 里的 records，借自客服后面查单时说的 according to our records——那是"按我们的记录"，与"为什么录音"毫不相干，是听到 records 就想选的原词陷阱。
optionAnalysis.C: 未提及：选项 To follow the company's rule. 说"为遵守公司规定"，录音里客服只说录音用于培训目的，从没提"规定/rule"这回事，属原文未提及。
optionAnalysis.D: 未提及：选项 To ensure information security. 说"为保障信息安全"，虽与客服场景的常识联想很近，但录音讲录音原因时只字未提"信息安全"，是按常识脑补出来的理由，原文无依据。
optionAnalysis.B: 正确项：与答案句同义替换（used in the future for training purposes ↔ For future training purposes. 几乎原句压缩）

questions.evidenceText: I just want to make you aware that this call is being recorded and may be used in the future for training purposes.

questions.stem: What is the woman's purpose of calling the furniture company?

options.text: To check her customer reference number.
To inquire about the price of office chairs.

transcript.text: A new study carried out by the University of Lincoln has found a link between the personalities of cat owners and the behaviour and wellbeing of their cats. The findings suggest that, just as a parent's personality can affect the personality of a child, the same is true for a cat and its owner.
transcript.zh: 林肯大学开展的一项新研究发现,猫主人的性格与其猫的行为和健康状况之间存在联系。研究结果表明,正如父母的性格会影响孩子的性格一样,猫和其主人之间也是如此。

transcript.text: Owners—defined as individuals with high levels of anxiety, fear, anger, depression and loneliness—were more likely to have cats with behavioural issues.
transcript.zh: 那些被定义为具有高度焦虑、恐惧、愤怒、抑郁和孤独感的主人,更有可能养出有行为问题的猫。

transcript.text: Such cats displayed more aggressive and anxious behavioural styles as well as more stress-related sickness. They were also more likely to have an ongoing medical condition and be overweight.
transcript.zh: 这些猫表现出更具攻击性和焦虑的行为方式,以及更多与压力相关的疾病。它们也更有可能患有持续性疾病和超重。

transcript.text: The research also found that mentally well-adjusted owners had calmer, happier and healthier cats.
transcript.zh: 研究还发现,心理健康状况良好的主人养的猫更平静、更快乐、更健康。

transcript.text: The researchers explained that "Many owners regard their pets as a family member, and form close social bonds with them." The majority of owners want to provide the best care for their pets and it's therefore possible that pets could be affected by the way their owners interact with and manage them. The study highlights an important relationship between our personalities and the wellbeing of our pets. Further research is needed to investigate the causal nature of this relationship and to look at how owners' personalities are directly influencing their pets' behaviour and wellbeing.
transcript.zh: 研究人员解释说,"许多主人将他们的宠物视为家庭成员,并与它们建立了紧密的社会联系。"大多数主人希望为他们的宠物提供最好的照顾,因此宠物可能会受到主人与它们互动和管理方式的影响。这项研究强调了我们的性格与宠物健康之间的重要关系。需要进一步研究来探讨这种关系的因果性质,以及主人的性格如何直接影响宠物的行为和健康状况。

transcript.text: It is possible that the wellbeing of pets is driven by the underlying nature of the owner, not simply by their conscious decisions and behaviours.
transcript.zh: 宠物的健康状况可能是由主人的内在本质驱动的,而不仅仅是由他们有意识的决定和行为驱动的。

transcript.text: "One 60-minute run can add seven hours to your life." This was a claim made by The Times last week. The claim was based on a new review of studies about the effects of running. The review concluded that on average runners live three years longer than non-runners and that running does more to extend life than any other form of exercise. But there's more to running than its health benefits. Research published in recent years has shown that running changes your brain and mind in some fascinating ways, from increasing your brain function to regulating your emotions. However, the precise effects vary according to whether you engage in short, fast running or long-distance running.
transcript.zh: "一次60分钟的跑步可以为你的生命增加7小时。"这是《泰晤士报》上周提出的一项声明。该声明基于一项关于跑步效果的新研究综述。该综述得出结论,跑步者平均比不跑步者多活3年,并且跑步比任何其他形式的运动都更能延长寿命。但跑步的意义不仅仅在于其健康益处。近年来发表的研究表明,跑步以一些引人入胜的方式改变你的大脑和思维,从提高大脑功能到调节情绪。然而,具体效果因你从事短距离快速跑步还是长距离跑步而异。

transcript.text: For example, in one study, researchers compared participants' ability to learn new words after several minutes of intense running and after 40 minutes of gentle running. Participants were able to learn 20 percent faster after the intense running and they showed a superior memory when tested again a week later.
transcript.zh: 例如,在一项研究中,研究人员比较了参与者在几分钟高强度跑步后和40分钟温和跑步后学习新单词的能力。参与者在高强度跑步后学习速度提高了20%,并且在一周后再次测试时表现出更优异的记忆力。

transcript.text: In another study, researchers asked volunteers to jog for 30 minutes and then showed them clips from a sad movie. Participants who usually struggled to handle negative emotions were more intensely affected by the sad clips, just as you'd expect. But crucially, this was less so if they had completed the 30-minute jog. The researchers said moderate exercise appears to have helped those participants to be less vulnerable to the impact of the sad movie.
transcript.zh: 在另一项研究中,研究人员要求志愿者慢跑30分钟,然后向他们播放悲伤电影的片段。通常难以处理负面情绪的参与者受到悲伤片段的影响更为强烈,正如你所预期的那样。但关键的是,如果他们完成了30分钟的慢跑,这种影响会有所减轻。研究人员表示,适度运动似乎帮助这些参与者减少了对悲伤电影影响的脆弱性。

questions.stem: What did the new review of studies claim?

options.text: People should do more running than mere walking.
Running is the best exercise for extending one's life.
People should exercise at least 60 minutes every day.
Running is the easiest form of exercise for most people.

questions.analysis: 细节题。答案句（P1）：The review concluded that on average runners live three years longer than non-runners and that running does more to extend life than any other form of exercise.信号：结论动词 concluded 领出的那句就是答案句 。录音里 The review concluded that 用 concluded（总结道）这个结论信号词领出综述的正式说法，结论信号后面跟的就是该研究 clai…

optionAnalysis.A: 原词陷阱：A 项 People should do more running than mere walking. 借了录音反复出现的 running 来诱选，但综述说的是跑步比其他运动更延寿，从没让人多跑少走，是听到 running 就想勾的原词陷阱。 借用原文：One 60-minute run can add seven hours to your life
optionAnalysis.C: 原词陷阱：C 项 People should exercise at least 60 minutes every day. 偷了开头 One 60-minute run 里的 60 分钟，但原文只是举例说一次 60 分钟的跑步，从没说每天至少运动 60 分钟，是把听到的数字硬塞进一个原文没有的主张。
optionAnalysis.D: 未提及：D 项 Running is the easiest form of exercise for most people. 听上去像常识，但综述比的是延寿效果（哪个更长寿），根本没比哪种运动最容易；easiest 是凭印象脑补出来的，原文未提。
optionAnalysis.B: 正确项：与答案句同义替换（running does more to extend life than any other form of exercise ↔ Running is the best exercise for extending one's life 比任何其他都强=最好，比较级升级为最高级）

questions.evidenceText: The review concluded that on average runners live three years longer than non-runners and that running does more to extend life than any other form of exercise.

questions.stem: What is one effect that running has on people according to recent research?
questions.analysis: 细节题。答案句（P1）：Research published in recent years has shown that running changes your brain and mind in some fascinating ways, from increasing your brain function to regulating your emotions.信号：shown that 引出近期研究结论，且与题干recent research对应 。录音 Research published in recent years has shown that 正对应题干里的 acco…

optionAnalysis.B: 原词陷阱：B 项 Regulating their breathing rate. 偷了录音里 regulating your emotions 的 regulating，但原文 regulating 后面跟的是 emotions（情绪），不是 breathing rate（呼吸频率）；它把对的动词配上错的对象，是张冠李戴式的原词陷阱。
optionAnalysis.C: 未提及：C 项 Slowing down their ageing process. 蹭了前文延长寿命的话题让人误以为有关衰老，但讲近期研究效果这句只提了脑功能和情绪，没说延缓衰老；属把别处话题挪过来的混淆。
optionAnalysis.D: 未提及：D 项 Accelerating their blood circulation. 是大家凭常识觉得跑步必然会有的效果，但录音讲的是改变大脑和心智（脑功能、情绪），完全没提血液循环，属常识代替原文。
optionAnalysis.A: 正确项：与答案句同义替换（increasing your brain function ↔ Improving their brain function increasing≈improving，brain function原义保留）

questions.evidenceText: Research published in recent years has shown that running changes your brain and mind in some fascinating ways, from increasing your brain function to regulating your emotions.

questions.stem: What did another study find about the participants after they had a 30-minute jog?

options.text: They found it easy to control their emotions.
They struggled to handle negative emotions.
They were more eager to enjoy a movie.
They were less affected by sad movies.

questions.analysis: 细节题。答案句（P3）：Participants who usually struggled to handle negative emotions were more intensely affected by the sad clips, just as you'd expect. But crucially, this was less so if they had completed the 30-minute jog.信号：转折But crucially之后才是真结论 。录音前半 were more intensely affected by the sad clips 是铺垫常态，真正的研究发现在转折词后：But crucially,…

optionAnalysis.B: 原词陷阱：B 项 They struggled to handle negative emotions. 几乎照搬录音 struggled to handle negative emotions 的原话，但那是描述被试平时（usually）的状态，不是慢跑后的发现；题干问的是慢跑之后，它答的是慢跑之前，是最毒的原词陷阱。 借用原文：less vulnerable to the impact of the sad movie
optionAnalysis.A: 过度推断：A 项 They found it easy to control their emotions. 把原文的受影响变小（less affected）夸成了能轻松控制情绪（easy to control），原文只说影响减弱，没说他们就能掌控情绪，是把程度推过了头。 借用原文：showed them clips from a sad movie
optionAnalysis.C: 原词陷阱：C 项 They were more eager to enjoy a movie. 借了录音里 movie 这个词，但原文讲的是被试被悲伤片段影响的程度，从没说他们更想看电影（eager to enjoy）；是借 movie 一词编出原文没有的内容。
optionAnalysis.D: 正确项：与答案句同义替换（this was less so if they had completed the 30-minute jog ↔ They were less affected by sad movies less so指回less affected，sad clips=sad movies）

questions.evidenceText: Participants who usually struggled to handle negative emotions were more intensely affected by the sad clips, just as you'd expect. But crucially, this was less so if they had completed the 30-minute jog.

transcript.text: Welcome to the tour of the Hill House. This house built in 1904 is one of the most well-known works of Charles Hill, the famous architect. It was designed and built for a local entrepreneur and his family. Before starting the tour, let me give you a brief introduction about the design of this amazing building.
transcript.zh: 欢迎参观Hill House。这座建于1904年的房子是著名建筑师Charles Hill最知名的作品之一。它是为一位当地企业家及其家人设计和建造的。在开始参观之前,让我简要介绍一下这座令人惊叹的建筑的设计。

transcript.text: Prior to beginning his design, the architect spent some time in the client's old home, observing their life and studying their habits. This meant that he could design the house according to the needs of the family.
transcript.zh: 在开始设计之前,建筑师在客户的老房子里待了一段时间,观察他们的生活并研究他们的习惯。这意味着他可以根据这个家庭的需求来设计房子。

transcript.text: The client's main desire was to have a home with the unique design, so the architect was given complete freedom. The building style is radically different from what was the fashion of the period. At the time, most large homes were constructed of timber and brick. This one, however, is made of concrete, a novel construction material in those days. The interior of the house, including fittings and furniture, was also designed by the same person. Most of the furniture you will see is original and in good condition. However, those pieces in the children's bedrooms are copies built to the designs of the architect. Fortunately, all the blueprints for both the building and its contents have been preserved, so we've been able to replace badly damaged furniture. Let's begin our tour, starting from the rooms.
transcript.zh: 客户的主要愿望是拥有一座设计独特的房子,因此建筑师获得了完全的自由。这座建筑的风格与当时的流行风格截然不同。那时,大多数大型住宅都是用木材和砖块建造的。然而,这座房子是用混凝土建造的,这在当时是一种新颖的建筑材料。房子的内部,包括装置和家具,也是由同一个人设计的。你将看到的大部分家具都是原件且保存完好。然而,儿童卧室里的那些家具是按照建筑师的设计建造的复制品。幸运的是,建筑及其内部陈设的所有蓝图都被保存了下来,所以我们能够更换严重损坏的家具。让我们开始参观吧,从这些房间开始。

questions.stem: What do we learn about the speaker?

options.text: He is the owner of the Hill House.

questions.analysis: 细节题。答案句（P1）：Welcome to the tour of the Hill House.信号：开场欢迎语暴露讲解员身份 。答案信号是录音第一句的开场套话 Welcome to the tour of the Hill House.——『欢迎来参观』这种带 tour 的欢迎词，只有带队讲解的人才会说，等于自报家…

optionAnalysis.B: 张冠李戴：录音确实念到 Charles Hill, the famous architect，但 famous architect 说的是设计这栋房子的查尔斯·希尔，不是正在讲解的说话人。选项 He is a famous architect. 把建筑师的身份安到了说话人头上，是典型的张冠李戴。 借用原文：a local entrepreneur and his family
optionAnalysis.C: 原词陷阱：It was designed and built for a local entrepreneur and his family. 里的 local entrepreneur（本地企业家）指的是当年请人盖房的客户，与说话人无关。选项 He is a local entrepreneur. 同样把客户的身份扣到说话人头上。
optionAnalysis.D: 未提及：录音只说房子是为 a local entrepreneur and his family 建的，从头到尾没说说话人是房主；带队做 tour 的讲解员通常也不是产权所有者。选项 He is the owner of the Hill House. 属未提及的臆测，原文无对应依据。
optionAnalysis.A: 正确项：与答案句同义替换（Welcome to the tour of the Hill House. ↔ He is a tour guide. 由动作反推身份）

questions.evidenceText: Welcome to the tour of the Hill House.

questions.stem: What did the architect do before beginning his design?

options.text: He studied the blueprints of other famous buildings.
He inquired about his client's family background.
He observed his client's life and habits.
He took a tour of his client's old home.

questions.analysis: 细节题。答案句（P2）：Prior to beginning his design, the architect spent some time in the client's old home, observing their life and studying their habits.信号：时间状语 Prior to 对上题干 before 。答案信号是时间状语 Prior to beginning his design——它和题干里的 before beginning his design 几乎一字不…

optionAnalysis.A: 原词陷阱：录音后文确实出现 all the blueprints for both the building and its contents have been preserved，blueprints（图纸）这个词被念到了，但那是说『这栋房子自己的图纸被保存下来』，并非建筑师设计前去研究『别家名建筑的图纸』。选项 He studied the blueprints of other famous buildings. 盗用 blueprints 一词，却凭空加了 other famous buildings，答非所问。 借用原文：a local entrepreneur and his family
optionAnalysis.B: 未提及：录音提到 client 和 family（a local entrepreneur and his family），让 family background 看着眼熟，但建筑师做的是『观察生活、研究习惯』，从没『inquired about family background（打听家世背景）』。inquire 这个动作录音根本没说，属未提及。 借用原文：spent some time in the client's old home
optionAnalysis.D: 原词陷阱：录音说建筑师 spent some time in the client's old home（在旧居里待了一段时间，目的是观察生活），并不是去 took a tour of his client's old home（参观一下旧居）。选项盗用 old home 一词，把『常驻观察』偷换成『参观一趟』，重点完全跑偏。
optionAnalysis.C: 正确项：与答案句同义替换（observing their life and studying their habits ↔ He observed his client's life and habits. 两个并列动作概括为一句）

questions.evidenceText: Prior to beginning his design, the architect spent some time in the client's old home, observing their life and studying their habits.

questions.stem: What did the architect's client mainly want?

options.text: A house made of timber and brick.
A house with a lot of free space.
A house of the current fashion.
A house of a unique design.

questions.analysis: 细节题。答案句（P3）：The client's main desire was to have a home with the unique design, so the architect was given complete freedom.信号：desire 直接点出客户愿望 。答案信号是表愿望的词 The client's main desire was——desire（愿望）与题干的 want 同义，直接领出客户到底想要什么。听到 desire / wa…

optionAnalysis.A: 原词陷阱：录音确实念到 most large homes were constructed of timber and brick，但这是在说『当时大多数大房子』的普遍做法，紧接着用 however 转折说这栋房子是用混凝土造的。选项 A house made of timber and brick. 盗用 timber and brick，描述的却是别家房子，不是客户想要的这栋。 借用原文：the architect was given complete freedom
optionAnalysis.B: 未提及：录音说 the architect was given complete freedom（建筑师获得完全的设计自由），freedom 与选项里的 free space 长得像、听起来也像，但 free space 指『大量空闲空间』，录音从没说客户想要宽敞空间。选项 A house with a lot of free space. 是利用 freedom / free 的相似制造混淆，属未提及。 借用原文：The building style is radically different from what was the fashion of the period
optionAnalysis.C: 与原文相反：录音明说 The building style is radically different from what was the fashion of the period（这栋房子的风格与当时的流行式样截然不同）。选项 A house of the current fashion. 盗用 fashion 一词，却把意思反了过来——客户要的恰恰是不随流行、独一无二，与原文意思相反。
optionAnalysis.D: 正确项：与答案句同义替换（a home with the unique design ↔ A house of a unique design. home 与 house 近义、措辞几乎照搬）

questions.evidenceText: The client's main desire was to have a home with the unique design, so the architect was given complete freedom.

questions.stem: What do we learn about the pieces of furniture in the children's bedrooms?

options.text: They are well preserved and in pretty good shape.
They are copies built to the architect's designs.
They were designed by another architect.
They were badly damaged but restored.

questions.analysis: 细节题。答案句（P3）：However, those pieces in the children's bedrooms are copies built to the designs of the architect.信号：However 转折锁定儿童房家具真相 。答案信号是转折词 However——前一句刚说大多数家具是原件、状况好，However 一转，专门交代『儿童房那批是复制品』。转折后正是题目问的那个对象的真相，这类题答案常落…

optionAnalysis.A: 张冠李戴：录音说 Most of the furniture you will see is original and in good condition——『状况好、是原件』讲的是『大多数家具』，紧接着 However 才转到儿童房那批是复制品。选项 They are well preserved and in pretty good shape. 把『大多数家具』的状态安到了题目问的『儿童房家具』头上，张冠李戴。 借用原文：copies built to the designs of the architect
optionAnalysis.C: 与原文相反：录音说儿童房家具是 copies built to the designs of the architect（按『这位建筑师』的图纸做的复制品），设计者就是本建筑师本人。选项 They were designed by another architect. 却说是『另一位建筑师』设计的，与原文意思相反。 借用原文：we've been able to replace badly damaged furniture
optionAnalysis.D: 原词陷阱：录音确实念到 we've been able to replace badly damaged furniture，badly damaged 这个词被说到了，但那是讲『靠保存下来的图纸去更换严重损坏的家具』，并不是说儿童房的家具被严重损坏后又修复了。选项 They were badly damaged but restored. 盗用 badly damaged，把它扣到儿童房家具上，对象与意思都错了。
optionAnalysis.B: 正确项：与答案句同义替换（those pieces in the children's bedrooms are copies built to the designs of the architect ↔ They are copies built to the architect's designs. 措辞几乎照搬，仅语序微调）

It is commonly believed that the great English dramatist and poet William Shakespeare was born in Stratford-on-Avon on April 23, 1564. But it is impossible to know the 26______ day on which he was born.

Church records show he was baptized(施洗礼) on April 26, and three days was a customary amount of time to wait before baptizing a newly born baby. Shakespeare's date of death is 27______ known, however: it was April 23, 1616. He was 52 and had retired to Stratford three years before.

Although few plays have been performed or analyzed as extensively as the 38 plays Shakespeare wrote, there are few surviving details about his life. This 28______ of biographical information is due primarily to his social 29______ ; he was not a noble, but the son of a leather trader.

Shakespeare 30______ attended the grammar school in Stratford, where he would have studied Latin and read 31______ literature. He did not go to university and at age 18 married Anne Hathaway, who was eight years his 32______ . They had four children, including the twins, Hamnet and Judith. Nothing is known of the period between the birth of the twins and Shakespeare's 33______ as a dramatist in London in the early 1590s.

In a million words written over 20 years, he 34______ the full range of human emotions and conflicts with a 35______ that remains sharp today. As his great contemporary the poet and dramatist Ben Jonson said, "He was not of an age, but for all time."

passages.title: Section B 长篇阅读匹配

paragraphs.label: A
paragraphs.text: Humans are creatures of habit. We love to establish a routine and stick with it. Then we often put ourselves on auto-pilot. Routines can be incredibly useful in helping you get things done. However, too much of a routine can also make you incredibly boring. Nevertheless, many people live lives that are boringly predictable, or live a life where everything is outlined or planned.

paragraphs.label: B
paragraphs.text: To tell the truth, interesting people are more popular among their friends. If you don't arouse someone's curiosity or brighten someone's day, you probably come across as being a little bit dull. But that doesn't mean your life has ended and you can't do anything to change it. If you find yourself searching for something to say beyond small talk, try these tactics to find more interesting approaches to conversation.

paragraphs.label: C
paragraphs.text: Recently, I was at a gathering of colleagues when someone turned to me and asked, "So, what's new with you?" Ordinarily, I think I'm a good conversationalist. After all, it's literally my job to talk to people and tell their stories or share their advice. And that's not exactly an unexpected question. Still, the only "new-to-me" topics that came to mind were my daughter's basketball tournament(锦标赛) and my feelings about that morning's political headlines—neither amusing nor appropriate topics at that moment.

paragraphs.label: D
paragraphs.text: Oh, no, I thought. Have I become boring? But sharing our experiences in an authentic way to connect with other people is what makes us interesting, says associate professor Michael Pirson. The hesitation I felt in not sharing the ordinary things that were happening in my life, and the wild mental search for something more interesting, may have backfired and made me seem less interesting.

paragraphs.label: E
paragraphs.text: "If someone is making up some conversation that might be interesting, it's probably not going to land well," says Pirson, whose expertise includes trust and well-being, mindfulness, and humanistic management. "It's going to feel like a made-up conversation that people don't necessarily want to tune in to."

paragraphs.label: F
paragraphs.text: The most interesting people aren't those who've gone on some Eat, Pray, Love journey to find themselves. Instead, Pirson says, they're those who examine the ordinary. "Often, the 'boring things' may not be boring at all. Maybe they are actually little miracles," he says. Share your observations about the world around you—interesting stories you heard or things you noticed—and you may be surprised by the universal connection they inspire.

paragraphs.label: G
paragraphs.text: This is essentially how Jessica Hagy starts her day. The author of How to Be Interesting: An Instruction Manual, Hagy spends a lot of time thinking about what's interesting to her. People who are interesting are persistently curious, she says.

paragraphs.label: H
paragraphs.text: Think about the everyday things around you and ask questions about them. What is that roadside monument I see on my way to work every day? Who built that interesting building in my city? What nearby attractions haven't I visited? Why do people do things that way? Use what you find to ask more questions and learn more about the world around you. "Having that sort of curiosity is almost like a protective gear from getting into boredom," she says. And when you find things that are truly interesting to you, share them.

paragraphs.label: I
paragraphs.text: Television veteran Audrey Morrissey, executive producer of NBC's The Voice, is always looking for what will make a person or story interesting to viewers: It's usually a matter of individuality. "Having a strong point of view, signature style, or being a super-enthusiast in a particular field makes someone interesting," she says. That means embracing what is truly interesting or unique about yourself. "Many people are 'not boring' in the way that they can carry a conversation or can be good at a social gathering, etc. To be interesting means that you have lived life, taken risks, traveled, sought out experience to learn for yourself and share with others," she says.

paragraphs.label: J
paragraphs.text: Of course, it's possible to be a fountain of knowledge and a boring person, says public relations consultant Andrea Pass. Paying attention to the listener is an important part of having a conversation that's interesting to both parties. Talking on and on about what's interesting to you isn't going to make you an interesting person, she says.

paragraphs.label: K
paragraphs.text: "If the listener is not paying attention, it's your sign to shorten the story or change direction. Make sure to bring the audience into the conversation so that it is not one-sided," Pass says. Be a better listener yourself, and give others opportunities to participate in the conversation by inviting them with questions or requests to share their own experiences or thoughts. (e.g., "Now, tell me about your favorite book," or "Have you ever been to that attraction?") Questions are a powerful tool, especially when they encourage others to disclose information about themselves. A 2012 study from the University of California, Santa Barbara, found that roughly 40% of the time we are talking, we're disclosing subjective information about our experience. And when we're doing so, our brains are more engaged. So one strategy to leave others with the impression that you're a sparkling conversation partner is to get others to talk about themselves.

paragraphs.label: L
paragraphs.text: Being relatable is also essential, Morrissey says. "The best entertainment and storytelling comes from people who are relatable-those who don't shy away from opening up but freely share who they are and what they care about. These are the people viewers most relate to and find interesting. Being authentic, honest, and vulnerable is always interesting."

paragraphs.label: M
paragraphs.text: I have now come to realize that being boring, in actuality, is not only about who you are as a person, but also how you present yourself. No matter what, make sure you are having fun in life. Because when you are enjoying, people around you will begin to enjoy as well. Show some interest in them and they will definitely show some in you. If you are a very reserved person, this could be a little difficult at first. But with a little effort, you can definitely improve.

Obesity, in which excess body fat has accumulated to such an extent that health may be adversely affected, meets the dictionary definition of disease, argues Professor John Wilding. He points out that more than 200 genes influence weight. "Thus body weight is strongly influenced by biology—it is not an individual's fault if they develop obesity." Yet the widespread view is that obesity is self-induced and that it is entirely the individual's responsibility to do something about it. Recognising obesity as a chronic disease with severe complications rather than a lifestyle choice "should help reduce the stigma(耻辱) and discrimination experienced by many people with obesity," he adds.
